Raw hex address 0x5040b6 assigned to bare local `uStack_220`. The decompiler dropped a symbolic reference — either a data-symbol pointer (recover the symbol from the .asm and replace `uStack_220` with symbolic global/array indexing, §11) or a dead code-address store from return-address tracking (delete it, §14). Magic addresses do not survive the relink.

Watcom field-by-field struct copy (3 consecutive `dst.field = src.field;` lines). Replace with `dst = src;` or `memcpy(&dst, &src, sizeof(...));` in a .keep — but only once the run (together with any sibling runs for the same dst/src pair) covers every byte of the struct. Collapsing a run that leaves a gap WIDENS the copy and changes behaviour; see `partial_struct_copy` (§31) for that case.

Watcom shadow-pointer walk — `pCStack_2c` self-updates via element-arithmetic `(int)(pCStack_2c + N) + M`, where `N*sizeof(*pCStack_2c) + M` equals the larger struct stride being walked (the pointer is typed to a sub-element). Replace `pCStack_2c->field` reads with direct indexing on the original pointer; drop the shadow init and self-update.

Watcom shadow-pointer walk — `pfStack_30` was initialized to the address of an array element's subfield (`pfStack_30 = &BASE->ARR[K].SUBFIELD;`) and is advanced here by `+ N` whole pointees, where `N * sizeof(*pfStack_30)` equals the array's element stride. The pointer is a smaller-typed walker striding a larger struct array. Replace the `pfStack_30->subfield` reads with direct indexing on the original array (`BASE->ARR[i].SUBFIELD`); drop the shadow init and advance.
